subtopicTitle: Chain rule for multivariable functions — all cases

cards.front: State the chain rule for dz/dt when z = f(x,y) with x = x(t), y = y(t).
State the chain rule for ζ/ζu when z = f(x,y) with x = x(u,v), y = y(u,v).
cards.back: $$\frac{\partial z}{\partial u} = \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u} + \frac{\partial f}{\partial y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}$$ (and likewise for ζ/ζv).

cards.front: Write the chain rule for ζ/ζt when z = f(x,y,w) and x,y,w each depend on t.
cards.back: $$\frac{dz}{dt} = \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\frac{dx}{dt} + \frac{\partial f}{\partial y}\frac{dy}{dt} + \frac{\partial f}{\partial w}\frac{dw}{dt}$$

cards.front: Give the general chain-rule formula for ζ/ζu_i when z = f(x_1,...,x_m) and each x_j = x_j(u_1,...,u_n).
cards.back: $$\frac{\partial z}{\partial u_i} = \sum_{j=1}^m \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_j} \frac{\partial x_j}{\partial u_i}$$

cards.front: Using the total differential, derive why the chain rule holds for z = f(x(u,v), y(u,v)).
cards.back: df = (ζf/ζx)dx + (ζf/ζy)dy. Divide by du (holding v fixed): ζf/ζu = (ζf/ζx)(ζx/ζu) + (ζf/ζy)(ζy/ζu).

cards.front: What changes in the chain rule when the outer function is vector-valued, F: R^2 	o R^2?
cards.back: Each component of F obeys its own scalar chain rule; the Jacobian matrix of the composition is the product of the individual Jacobians.

cards.front: Edge case: when does the multivariable chain rule reduce to the ordinary single-variable chain rule?
cards.back: When the outer function depends on only one intermediate variable (all other partials vanish) or when all inner functions depend on a single parameter t.

cards.front: Intuitive explanation: why must every path through the dependency tree be summed?
cards.back: A small change in an independent variable reaches the output along every possible route; the total effect is the linear sum of the effects along each route (first-order approximation).
